Finally, continuous monitoring of relevant physiological signals, through developing algorithms, have the potential for early prediction of clinical deterioration. Non-invasive, co-created digital solutions may facilitate early stabilisation, improve functional capacity and predict clinical deterioration following episodes of decompensation. Collectively, they may enhance clinical outcomes and quality of life in patients with HF.

articles.title: Hybrid Airway Management for Neuromonitoring-guided Selective Phrenic Nerve Surgery in Intractable Hiccups: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: Intractable hiccups are rare but debilitating, and may cause sleep disturbances, nutritional impairment, exhaustion, and a severe deterioration in quality of life. When pharmacological and interventional treatments fail, selected surgical procedures targeting the phrenic nerve may be considered. We report the anaesthetic management of a 32-year-old woman with idiopathic intractable hiccups who underwent right-sided selective phrenic nerve surgery guided by thoracoscopic neuromonitoring. Because thoracoscopic exposure and intraoperative neuromonitoring were required simultaneously, a hybrid airway strategy combining an electromyography endotracheal tube with a bronchial blocker was used. The patient was positioned in the left lateral decubitus position, and the bronchial blocker was placed in the right main bronchus under fiberoptic bronchoscopic guidance. One-lung ventilation was maintained for 35 minutes with FiO2 of 0.70 to 0.80, tidal volume of 5-6 mL kg-1, respiratory rate of 18 min-1, and PEEP of 5 cmH2O; the arterial blood gas analysis at 25 minutes showed pH 7.38, PaCO2 41 mmHg, and PaO2 92 mmHg. Sugammadex was administered intraoperatively to restore diaphragmatic motor responses required for branch-specific neuromonitoring. The medial and anterolateral branches of the right phrenic nerve exhibited abnormal electrophysiological responses and were treated with selective bipolar ablation and clipping. Postoperatively, the patient remained on room air, reported no intraoperative recall, and showed no clinically relevant diaphragmatic dysfunction on clinical and functional assessment. This case illustrates that established anaesthetic techniques can be carefully adapted to meet the competing requirements of lung isolation, anaesthetic depth control, and neuromonitoring in selected patients undergoing phrenic nerve surgery for intractable hiccups.

articles.title: Comparison of Postoperative Analgesic Efficacy Between Opioid-free Anaesthesia Using Intravenous Magnesium, Lidocaine, and Erector Spinae Plane Block, and Opioid-based Anaesthesia in Laparoscopic Abdominal Surgeries: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: Opioid-based anaesthesia is a standard practice in laparoscopic surgeries. However, it is associated with adverse effects that can limit its use. To address these issues, opioid-free anaesthesia has been introduced as an alternative. This study aims to compare the analgesic efficacy of opioid-free anaesthesia, incorporating magnesium, lidocaine, and an erector spinae plane block (ESPB), with traditional opioid-based anaesthesia during laparoscopic procedures. Seventy patients aged 18-60 years undergoing laparoscopic surgery were randomly divided into two groups of 35 each. Opioid-free group received opioid-free anaesthesia, which included an intravenous (IV) bolus of 2 g magnesium, a continuous lidocaine infusion at 1.5 mg kg-1 hr-1, and a bilateral ESPB with 25 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine. Opioid-based group received opioid-based anaesthesia with an IV dose of 2 μg kg-1 fentanyl. Postoperative pain and the need for rescue analgesia were assessed for 24 h. Perioperative haemodynamic parameters were recorded, and the incidence of postoperative complications, including sedation, nausea, vomiting, and shivering, was monitored for 24 h. Pain scores were significantly lower in the opioid-free group compared to the opioid-based group at 0 h (P < 0.001), 2 h (P < 0.001), and 4 h (P=0.005) postoperatively. The opioid-based group required rescue analgesia more frequently (P < 0.001). Additionally, the incidence of postoperative complications was significantly lower in the opioid-free group than in the opioid-based group (P < 0.001). Haemodynamic parameters were similar between the two groups. Opioid-free anaesthesia provides superior postoperative analgesia and reduces the incidence of postoperative complications compared with opioid-based anaesthesia for laparoscopic surgery.

articles.title: Harnessing the Power of Education for a Low-carbon Future in Anaesthesia: A Narrative Review.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: Climate change poses a significant threat to public health, with the healthcare sector being a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions. Anaesthesia and the operating room are notable contributors within this sector, particularly because of volatile inhalation gases such as desflurane and nitrous oxide. Therefore, improving sustainability in anaesthesia is a clinical and ethical imperative. This review examines recent advances in leveraging education to promote low-carbon anaesthesia practices. We summarize evidence on how various educational interventions and formats can reduce the carbon footprint of anaesthesia and discuss implementation strategies, challenges, and future directions. Many studies demonstrate that educational programs reduce the use of high global warming potential anaesthetic agents. Programs vary widely in scope, ranging from single-session lectures and surveys to multi-year sustainability task forces and formal policy changes, some of which have resulted in up to a 90% reduction in volatile agent emissions. Combining multiple techniques (such as lectures, posters, and vaporizer labeling) has been associated with substantial reductions in volatile agent emissions and with improved organizational readiness for sustainability initiatives. These education-driven shifts toward environmentally friendly approaches, such as low-flow techniques, total intravenous anaesthesia, and regional anaesthesia, have proven effective, cutting costs, maintaining patient safety, and reducing carbon emissions. Educational initiatives represent a practical and cost‑efficient strategy to reduce carbon emissions in anaesthesia practice and in healthcare. By integrating environmental stewardship into anaesthesia training and policy, anaesthesiologists can lead the transition of healthcare to low-carbon care.

articles.title: The Analgesia Nociception Index is More Strongly Associated with Anxiety Than with Pain in Conscious Male Patients Undergoing Hernia Repair Under Combined Spinal-epidural Anaesthesia.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: The Analgesia Nociception Index (ANI), derived from heart rate variability, is a non-invasive marker of the nociception- analgesia balance. Its validity and validity in conscious are uncertain because activity may also psychological factors, particularly anxiety. This exploratory study examined the among ANI, pain, and anxiety in male patients undergoing hernia repair with combined spinal-epidural anaesthesia (CSEA). Twenty-four male patients with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I-II undergoing hernia repair under CSEA were enrolled. Self-reported visual analogue scale for Anxiety (VAS-A), pain (VAS), and continuously recorded ANI were assessed at four procedural stages: lateral positioning (T1), local anaesthetic infiltration (T2), epidural puncture (T3), and two minutes post-puncture (T4). Within-patient (primary), patient-level, and observation-level correlations were and the two within-patient correlations involving ANI were formally compared. At the within-patient level, ANI correlated negatively with anxiety (r=-0.794, P < 0.001) and with pain (r=-0.515, P < 0.001); the ANI-stronger than the ANI-pain correlation. The association between ANI and anxiety was significantly stronger than that between ANI and pain (Hotelling-Williams t=4.10, P < 0.001). The patient-level ANI--pain analysis was clearly underpowered (post-hoc power ≈ 0.18). Clinicians should therefore avoid interpreting a low ANI value as evidence of inadequate analgesia alone and should consider concurrent assessment of both pain and anxiety. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, sex-balanced, multicentre studies. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05053633), registered 22 September 2021.

articles.title: Low-Angle Paramedian Approach versus Midline Approach for Remote Access Epidural Blood Patch: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: While mid-thoracic CSF leaks (T7-T8) require targeted epidural blood patches, direct thoracic puncture carries a significant risk of spinal cord injury due to the narrow epidural space. To mitigate this risk, a safety-oriented remote-access strategy from the T12-L1 level, with cranial advancement of the catheter, was employed to prevent direct thoracic spinal cord injury. We present a 46-year-old male with a T7-T8 leak in whom a standard midline approach failed due to poor catheter steerability. By adopting a low-angle (<30°) paramedian approach, we achieved precise ipsilateral catheter positioning; this technical modification provides optimized vector alignment and a tangential epidural trajectory for unilateral thoracic leaks. This technical modification may improve maneuverability and safety for unilateral thoracic leaks, compared to standard midline techniques, and appears to facilitate an optimized tangential trajectory in this case.

articles.title: Trends in the Use of Neuraxial vs. General Anaesthesia for Transurethral Resection of the Prostate.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: Historically, neuraxial anaesthesia (NA) was preferred for transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) to allow monitoring for TURP syndrome, but modern surgical techniques have largely eliminated this risk. We aimed to characterise trends in anaesthesia utilisation for TURP over a 15-year period and to identify patient factors associated with anaesthetic technique selection. We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing primary TURP using the ACS-NSQIP database (2009-2023). Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of the use of general anaesthesia (GA) versus NA. Subgroup analyses examined trends by patient health status and age. Of 73,214 patients identified, GA utilisation increased significantly from 69.9% in 2009 to 88.8% in 2023 (P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, each successive year was associated with a 15% increase in the odds of receiving GA [odds ratio (OR) 1.15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.14-1.15]. Black patients (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.47-1.87) had higher odds of GA than white patients, and hispanic patients (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.38-1.64) had higher odds of GA than non-hispanic patients. Conversely, older age, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.71-0.84), and diabetes (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.93) were associated with decreased GA use. The shift towards GA was significantly more pronounced among medically complex patients (American Society of Anesthesiologists 3-4) than among less medically complex patients (P=0.005). The anaesthetic management of TURP has evolved over the last 15 years, and GA has further solidified its status as the dominant modality. This evolution likely reflects the diminished risk of TURP syndrome, allowing practice to be driven by airway control and efficiency rather than by historical safety constraints.

articles.title: One-Lung Ventilation for Neonatal Pneumonectomy in a Hydropic Premature Infant: Fiberoptic-guided Left Mainstem Intubation.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: Congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation (CCAM) is a rare lung anomaly that can cause severe respiratory distress and hydrops fetalis. One-lung ventilation (OLV) in neonates poses extreme anatomical challenges due to the lack of appropriately sized double-lumen tubes or bronchial blockers. A male neonate (2500 g, 30 weeks' gestation) presented with hydrops fetalis and a massive right-sided thoracic CCAM. Due to progressive respiratory failure and hemodynamic instability, an emergency right pneumonectomy was scheduled on postnatal day 3. To achieve OLV, a 3.5-mm cuffed endotracheal tube (with the cuff left deflated) was advanced into the left main bronchus under fiberoptic bronchoscopy (FOB) guidance. Removal of the tube adaptor facilitated rapid, pragmatic placement while minimizing interruptions to ventilation during apneic oxygenation. Pressure-controlled lung-protective ventilation was maintained. Transient desaturation episodes during mediastinal manipulation were successfully managed. The 3-hour procedure was completed without intraoperative complications. In premature neonates in whom commercial lung-isolation devices are impractical, FOB-guided selective mainstem bronchial intubation is a rapid, feasible, and effective strategy for OLV. Individualized airway planning and FOB guidance are instrumental in ensuring accurate placement and maintaining oxygenation.

articles.title: Adaptability of Medical Surge Preparedness Practices to Large-Scale Combat Operations.
articles.abstract: Since its inception, the National Disaster Medical System (NDMS) has been activated in the context of acute-onset and time-limited disasters; however, its original intended purpose was for providing care for casualties from a large-scale combat operation (LSCO). Consequently, determining the utility of specific medical surge practices for an LSCO is necessary to optimally prepare the NDMS for such an event. Lessons learned from prior medical surge events can inform LSCO preparations despite the contextual differences between the 2 scenarios. This case study builds on earlier analyses by the US Department of Defense's NDMS Pilot program to develop a set of evidence-based leading practices for improving medical surge response that can be used by healthcare facilities providing acute care during LSCO-related patient surges.

articles.title: Ultra-high-resolution photon-counting CT argues against a suspected bilateral carotid web: a case report.
articles.abstract: Carotid web is diagnosed almost entirely from a shelf-like filling defect at CT angiography (CTA), yet the posterolateral carotid bulb at which webs arise is also a site of flow separation in which blood of differing contrast density mixes. We describe a bilateral web-like appearance at this site and determine whether it arose from reconstruction or acquisition. A 75-year-old woman with a right-hemispheric transient ischemic attack had three carotid CTA examinations: a dual-energy energy-integrating-detector CT (EID-CT) angiogram five months before presentation, a stroke-protocol photon-counting-detector CT (PCD-CT) angiogram at presentation, and a dedicated ultra-high-resolution PCD-CT angiogram three days later. Each photon-counting acquisition was additionally reconstructed with other section thicknesses, kernels or energies, and attenuation across the appearance was measured. A bilateral shelf-like filling defect closely simulating a carotid web was present on the EID-CT and presenting PCD-CTF angiograms but absent on the ultra-high-resolution study. The tested reconstructions neither abolished the appearance nor elicited it. The ultra-high-resolution study was acquired 16.6 s after the end of injection at less than half the table speed, versus 10.3 s on the presenting study. Attenuation at the corresponding position measured 62%, 54% and 87% of luminal attenuation, respectively. No carotid intervention was undertaken. An acquisition-dependent bilateral carotid bulb pseudolesion can mimic a carotid web on both EID-CT and PCD-CT angiography and is most consistent with flow-related mixing of blood of differing contrast density. A slower repeat acquisition of the carotid bulb with a few seconds more delay may prevent unnecessary revascularization.

articles.title: A narrative review of CBRN health sector preparedness in Lebanon.
articles.abstract: As chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) events become increasingly recognised within international and national emergency preparedness efforts, this study aims to provide the first system-level overview of Lebanon's preparedness capacities for CBRN-related health emergencies. A narrative review of peer-reviewed and grey literature was conducted using a structured search strategy, with findings thematically synthesised to assess governance and operational CBRN preparedness capacities across eight health system domains in Lebanon. The review identified important advances in Lebanon's preparedness for CBRN health emergencies, including engagement with international preparedness frameworks, development of governance structures, and implementation of coordination, training, and simulation initiatives. However, preparedness remains uneven and constrained by fragmented coordination, legislative gaps, limited surveillance and operational integration, shortages in material and human resources, and dependence on external support. Economic instability and workforce migration further challenge sustainability, while preparedness capacities and readiness levels vary across emergency response and healthcare institutions. Overall, strategic planning and governance capacities appeared stronger than operational response and surveillance functions. While major efforts towards CBRN preparedness in Lebanon have been initiated, key aspects remain under-developed. Given Lebanon's continued exposure to recurrent crises and regional instability, strengthening CBRN preparedness should be considered a critical component of broader health system resilience and national disaster risk reduction efforts.

articles.title: Development and independent regional validation of a dynamic ultrasound appendicitis score for suspected acute appendicitis: a prospective multicenter study.
articles.abstract: Acute appendicitis is the most common surgical emergency. Although CT is highly accurate, radiation exposure is a major concern in children, young adults, and pregnant women. Ultrasound is radiation-free but operator-dependent, and current scores rely on static weights without accounting for important patient-finding interactions. To develop and independently validate a Dynamic Ultrasound Appendicitis Score (Dynamic UAS) with interaction effects to improve risk stratification and potentially avoid unnecessary CT examinations. A prospective multicenter study collected development (n = 802) and independent regional external validation (n = 262) data. The Dynamic UAS was derived using multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms and internally validated using bootstrapping (1000 resamples). A web-based calculator was developed. A sensitivity analysis addressed limitations of the reference standard, non-visualized appendix, and missing data. Appendicitis prevalence was 33.3% (development) and 32.8% (validation). The Dynamic UAS performed excellently in diagnosing acute appendicitis (AUC 0.96 and 0.94) and outperformed known scores (AUC 0.81 to 0.91). At the ≥ 6 level, sensitivity was 91.7%/90.7%, and specificity was 97.1%/96.0%. Calibration was good (slope 0.89, Brier 0.098). In non-visualized appendix cases, the AUC was 0.89 (95% CI: 0.84 to 0.93) in the external validation cohort and 0.90 (95% CI: 0.85 to 0.94) in the development cohort. The model is not very useful for distinguishing complicated from uncomplicated appendicitis (AUC 0.72). The Dynamic UAS is a novel, independently validated tool that may reduce unnecessary CT use in radiation-sensitive populations and resource-limited settings. Future studies in different international settings are needed.

articles.title: Comparison of Acute Physiology, Age and Chronic Health Evaluation II score and Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning Scale in predicting clinical outcomes and mortality in organophosphorus poisoning.
articles.abstract: Organophosphorus poisoning is a major health hazard in developing countries. We conducted a study to compare the Acute Physiology, Age and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) scoring system and Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning Scale in predicting the complications, ventilator requirement and mortality in patients of Acute Organophosphorus Poisoning. A prospective observational study was done on 100 patients above 18 years of age, presenting with alleged history of consumption of organophosphorus compounds. The patients were evaluated for the required details to calculate the APACHE II score and Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning Scale and were followed up till discharge or mortality to identify the complications, ventilator requirement and mortality. This data was tabulated using Excel and analyzed using SPSS software to look for correlation between the scores and the outcome. The mean age of our patients was 33.64 ± 12.99 years. The APACHE II cutoff score for complications, ventilator requirement and mortality was ≥ 7 (sensitivity 94.3%, specificity 96.9%, Area under Receiver Operator Characteristic (ROC) 0.99, p < 0.01), ≥9 (sensitivity 86.7%, specificity 82.4%, Area under ROC 0.91, p < 0.01) and ≥16 (sensitivity 85.7, specificity 96.8%, Area under ROC 0.98, p < 0.01) respectively. Similarly, the Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning Scale cutoff was for complications, ventilator requirement and mortality was ≥ 3 (sensitivity 80%, specificity 92.3%, Area under ROC 0.90, p < 0.01), ≥3 (sensitivity 80%, specificity 75.3%, Area under ROC 0.85, p < 0.01) and ≥7 (sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 97.8%, Area under ROC 0.99, p < 0.01) respectively. Both APACHE II and POPS demonstrated good predictive performance for adverse outcomes in acute organophosphorus poisoning. Both scores showed excellent discrimination for mortality, with no statistically significant difference between their AUCs.

articles.title: Psychometric evaluation of the Persian version of the shared decision‑making questionnaire in patients undergoing emergency surgery.
articles.abstract: Accurate assessment of shared decision-making (SDM) is essential in emergency surgery, yet no culturally adapted and validated instrument is available in Iran. This study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and assess the psychometric properties of the Persian SDM-Q-9 among patients undergoing emergency surgery. This methodological cross-sectional study followed a forward-backward translation procedure to adapt the SDM-Q-9 into Persian. Face and content validity were established prior to construct validation. Data were collected from 575 patients undergoing emergency surgery and randomly split into two independent subsamples for exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 287) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 288). Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha, McDonald's omega, and composite reliability (CR). Convergent validity was examined using average variance extracted (AVE). The data were suitable for factor analysis (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin [KMO] = 0.923; Bartlett's test of sphericity: χ² = 3433.445, df = 36, p < 0.001). EFA using Maximum Likelihood (ML) extraction with Promax rotation supported a single-factor structure explaining 58.60% of the total variance, with all factor loadings exceeding 0.70. CFA of the independent validation subsample initially showed inadequate fit for the one-factor model. After reviewing modification indices and item content, three theoretically justified residual correlations were retained. The resulting model showed good fit (χ²/df = 2.78, Comparative Fit Index [CFI] = 0.962, Tucker-Lewis Index [TLI] = 0.944, Root Mean Square Error of Approximation [RMSEA] = 0.059, and Standardized Root Mean Square Residual [SRMR] = 0.052). Factor loadings ranged from 0.67 to 0.84, supporting a predominantly unidimensional structure. The scale demonstrated strong internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.921, McDonald's omega = 0.926, and CR = 0.924). Convergent validity was supported by an AVE of 0.576. The Persian SDM-Q-9 demonstrated satisfactory validity and strong reliability for assessing patient-perceived shared decision-making in emergency surgical settings in Iran. Its predominantly unidimensional structure supports its use, although the localized residual associations identified in CFA warrant replication in independent, multicenter samples.

articles.title: Three doors, three locks: a domain-specific framework for the residual door-to-balloon gap in STEMI care : Matters Arising, commentary on Krishnan et al., Int J Emerg Med 2026;19:113.
articles.abstract: Krishnan and colleagues report that 91% of STEMI patients at a large Indian tertiary centre received primary PCI within the 90-minute door-to-balloon (D2B) target, a meaningful achievement in contemporary STEMI care. Their analysis of the 9% who missed the target is equally valuable: delays distributed almost evenly across three categories, delayed informed consent, hemodynamic instability, and diagnostic ambiguity. We argue these categories are not interchangeable quality-improvement targets. They are mechanistically distinct problems requiring different solutions. We propose a conceptual, hypothesis-generating framework rather than a validated taxonomy. Future STEMI quality improvement efforts should categorize residual delays by domain rather than reporting them in aggregate, and should match interventions to the specific mechanism of delay.

articles.title: Securing Medical Countermeasures in Public Health Emergencies.
Strangulated Posterior Rectus Sheath Hernia with Contained Small-Bowel Perforation and Abdominal Wall Necrotizing Infection: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Posterior rectus sheath hernia is an exceptionally uncommon interparietal hernia and may be difficult to recognize because the herniated bowel remains between abdominal wall layers. A 49-year-old multiparous woman presented with acute severe pain, vomiting, fever, and inflammatory skin changes over a right paraumbilical swelling that had been present for six years. Ultrasound suggested a complicated abdominal wall cyst, whereas computed tomography demonstrated a right rectus sheath hernia. Emergency exploration revealed strangulated and perforated small bowel contained between rectus sheath layers, with enteric leakage into necrotic anterior abdominal wall tissues. Approximately 20 cm of gangrenous bowel was resected and a primary end-to-end anastomosis was performed. The small fascial defect was closed primarily without mesh because of the dirty infected field. The skin and subcutaneous wound were left open after debridement, managed with temporary packing and two further operative debridements, and closed secondarily after infection control. The patient recovered and was discharged in good clinical condition. Posterior rectus sheath hernia should be considered in atypical abdominal wall masses. Early computed tomography and urgent source control are essential when strangulation, perforation, or necrotizing infection is suspected.

articles.title: Early-Phase Computed Tomography Bowel Diameter and Neurological Outcomes Post-Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.
articles.abstract: We aimed to conduct an exploratory investigation on the association between bowel diameter on early-phase abdominal computed tomography (CT) and neurological outcomes in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). This observational study included patients who underwent ECPR for OHCA and abdominal CT before intensive care unit admission between January 2015 and December 2021 at a tertiary emergency medical center. Maximum bowel diameter was measured with a picture archiving and communication system by an investigator blinded to outcomes. The primary endpoint was unfavorable neurological outcomes at 1 month, defined as Cerebral Performance Category 3-5. The discriminatory ability of bowel diameter was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Data from 181 patients were analyzed (median age, 57 years; 84.5% male). Bowel diameter demonstrated a weak ability to predict unfavorable neurological outcomes, with an AUC of 0.58 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47-0.70). However, higher discriminatory performance was observed in subgroups of patients aged ≥ 65 years (AUC, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.69-0.96) and those with initial nonshockable rhythms (AUC, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.47-0.91). The results of this exploratory investigation suggest that bowel diameter may represent a potential adjunctive marker associated with functional outcomes post-ECPR for OHCA.
